# Project Properties

Open **Project Properties** from **Window → Editors** to edit settings stored
in the current `.blue` project. Application-wide defaults and the local
audio or MIDI devices are in [Settings](settings.qmd). Keeping device choices
outside the project makes it easier to move a project between computers.

## Project Information

**Title**, **Author**, and **Notes** identify the project. They also provide
the descriptive header in generated CSD. Use this tab for information about
the composition rather than Csound code.

## Realtime

Set the project sample rate, `ksmps`, channel count, and optional `0dbfs`
value for realtime playback. **Use Audio Out/In** and **Use MIDI In/Out**
control which I/O the project requests. The **Note Amps**, **Out Of Range**,
**Warnings**, and **Benchmark** switches control Csound's message level.

**Advanced Settings** adds Csound option flags. **Complete Override** uses
that text as the real-time Csound option list instead of Blue's normal
audio/MIDI, device, buffer, and message-level options. Add any required driver
and device flags to the override. The project's sample rate, `ksmps`, channel
count, and `0dbfs` remain in the generated CSD orchestra header. **Project →
Generate CSD to Screen** shows that header but not the real-time launch
options. Without an override, device and buffer choices come from
[Settings](settings.qmd).

## Disk Render

Disk rendering has its own sample rate, `ksmps`, channels, `0dbfs`, message
level, and advanced options. In normal mode, **File Name** provides the
project output path and **Ask on Render** prompts for a destination each time.
**Disk Complete Override** uses the Disk Advanced Settings text as the full
Csound option list; include an output `-o` path there. In override mode, Blue
does not use **File Name** or **Ask on Render**. **Render Entire Project**
ignores a selected Score range for disk output. See [Rendering](rendering.qmd)
for the render controls and output behavior.

## Media

**Media Folder** sets where imported assets are copied. A relative path is
resolved from the project directory; an absolute path is used directly. When
the field is blank, Blue uses a `media` folder beside the project. Prefer a
relative path when moving the project and its assets together. **Copy Imported
Media** controls whether supported imports are copied there; when it is off,
the project refers to the source files. Changing this setting does not move
assets imported earlier, so verify their paths when sharing the project.

The **Clojure** tab lists project libraries by dependency coordinates and
version. Blue loads these dependencies for the project's Clojure content
before evaluation and rendering. Keep the list aligned with the dependencies
expected by that content; use **Add Library**, **Move Up**, **Move Down**, and
**Remove** to maintain it.
